rule: Full columns of 6 split the grid into one or two narrow legend strips and one strictly wider canvas strip; the output is the canvas. Each legend's upper area (background 0) holds a solid two-colour tile and a one-colour shape. Below are two 6-framed 3x3 boxes: a 4 in box 1 marks the anchor corner, and a centre 7 plus an edge 7 in box 2 form the arrow. The shape is rotated by the arrow (up = identity, down = 180, right = clockwise, left = counter-clockwise). Each rotated-shape cell becomes one copy of the tile with its two colours swapped; the tile itself is not rotated. The result is placed flush in the anchor corner of the canvas, and non-shape cells keep the canvas colours.
scope: One or two instruction legends specify a shape rotation, unrotated colour-swapped tile, and canvas anchor. Random tight asymmetric shapes, solid/banded/cross/blob canvases, square or rectangular tiles, observable anchors, and optional hard tile decisions.
constraints: All five canonical examples reconstruct exactly. 1000 independent seeds pass the archived input-only solver.

An independent pixel decoder for separator columns, two-colour tiles, connected masks, arrow cells and anchor cells passes 1645 distinct scenes. It checks 360 single-legend canvas shapes, 220 combinations of tile size and legend side, and 60 fixed-canvas scenes.

All 2084 synthetic legends have observable anchor coordinates and asymmetric shape masks; the six canonical legends are checked separately and retain their broader scope. Across all scenes, 2030 tiles distinguish colour swap from every D4 image and 232 tiles are rectangular.
Forced hard_tile=True cases distinguish colour swap from geometric transforms and make non-up tile rotation observable. Maximum tile size25 cells and shape size47 cells.
Twelve invalid controls reject promptly, including float dimensions with explicit canvas and an impossible legend-width request. Critic retest passes25 valid and10 rejection cases.
known_limitations: Legend widths4..7, grid width11..30, default height13..30 subject to tile fit; single tile side5 and two-legend side<=4. Fixed separator/frame colour6, anchor4, arrow7.
Random shapes are asymmetric and stamps do not overlap. Explicit fixtures retain symmetric shapes and ambiguous tiles; not every canonical ambiguity is sampled by the hard subset.
Rectangular tiles and alternative top-area layouts are synthetic extensions; their validity is based on the stated rule and independent/reference checks, not new benchmark demonstrations.
Hard tiles are sampled with a declared85% per-legend probability before feasibility filtering, not an asserted final frequency. The paper should report achieved distributions.
billing: Claude Max CLI; API credentials excluded; no API fallback

authored_scope:
Supported:
- One left, one right, or one left plus one right legend. Legends are 4..7 wide in random scenes.
- Square tiles of side 2..5, plus about 25% rectangular tiles when tile_size is None.
- Tile above shape, shape above tile, or the two side by side.
- Asymmetric 4- or 8-connected random shapes.
- All four arrows and all four anchors. Two legends always have distinct anchors and non-overlapping stamps.
- Solid, banded, cross and blob canvases. Supplied canvases are also accepted.
- Random heights (tile_size+11)..30, which is 13..30 by default, and total widths 11..30.
- The hard_tile control: tile swap is not a D4 image, and tile non-rotation is observable for non-up arrows.

Explicit legends reconstruct the canonical fixtures and accept a wider canonical-compatible scope: height 9..30, symmetric shapes, ambiguous tiles, tile colours shared with the canvas, and stamps spanning the full canvas.

Not supported:
- More than two legends, or legends above or below the canvas.
- A box layout other than H = separator + 8.
- Hollow or non-solid tiles.
- Tiles that rotate with the arrow.
authored_constraints: Exactly one strip between full-6 columns is strictly the widest (the canvas). No full-6 column or full-6 row occurs except the dividers and the two legend band rows.
Canvas never contains 6. Random tile colours are absent from the canvas, and two legends use four distinct tile colours.
The tile is solid and contains exactly two colours. The shape colour differs from both tile colours.
Tile and shape do not touch, even diagonally. The tile lies outside the shape bounding box.
Random shape masks are tight, connected and fully asymmetric under D4. Masks are at least 2x3.
Random stamps are strictly smaller than the canvas in both height and width, so the anchor choice affects the output.
Two-legend stamps never overlap, and their anchors are distinct.

Hard tiles: the colour-swapped tile is not in the D4 orbit of the tile, and rotate(tile, arrow) != tile for non-up arrows. Tiles of 9 cells or fewer are drawn from an enumerated valid-pattern list; larger tiles use bounded rejection.
The output differs from the canvas. Explicit scenes that leave the canvas unchanged are rejected.
Integer controls must be plain ints. When a canvas is supplied, height and width are type-checked before they are compared with it.

Infeasible control combinations raise ValueError before sampling: width versus the real legend width bounds of a supplied canvas, tile_size 5 with two legends, height below tile_size+11, and too few free palette colours. Malformed explicit tiles raise ValueError before any palette is built.
